what_each_control_actually_fails.reuse_bypassed: test_prefix_reuse_witness — 0 hits and 0 queries on all eight prefixes
what_each_control_actually_fails.reuse_state_corruption: STOCHASTICALLY, and only through test_api_probes. Three full observations of this control: the 14-minute probe and one full trial failed test_api_probes on greedy determinism (the same divergent continuation, word for word); a third trial passed every node. The probe catches the fault only when its repeated greedy request is served from a cache hit on the corrupted state, which the probe does not control. The agreement node never separates it: zeroing the PLE convolution state for a handful of tokens moves the first generated token by about 1e-8, inside the correct server's own warm-versus-cold noise. Recorded as a finding; no bar or case was changed to make this control fail.

fidelity_T.statistic: the largest LENGTH-BAND median of the per-sequence mean k3; the whole-set median is reported beside it and is NOT the gate (a control confined to one regime moves only part of the population and a single median is blind to it -- measured: qsa_recent_only raised the 12,288 band to 454.6 while the whole-set median stayed at 0.052)

fidelity_T.note: The 18,432-token band is ABOVE the recipe's max_num_batched_tokens of 16,384 and is the only input in the whole verifier that forces a chunked prefill. It is also the quietest band, which is the finding: chunked prefill at this landing agrees with the reference reference implementation about three times more closely than a single-chunk 512-token sequence does.

bars.prefix_reuse_T2_design: The cases are 784*pages + tail with tail between 2 and 8 tokens, so the first GENERATED token sits inside the PLE convolution's ten-token receptive field of the cache boundary. The first design used round lengths whose tails were 176 to 784 tokens; the scored position was then hundreds of tokens past the boundary, the oracle's own warm-versus-cold k3 spanned 1e-5 to 23, and the oracle tripped the node's top-5 assertion on two runs of five. On the redesigned cases the oracle sits at 1e-14 to 3.5e-7. The top-5 rule and the agreed-run length are DIAGNOSTICS for the same reason: measured, they do not separate the reuse_state_corruption control from a correct server.
bars.prefix_reuse_page_note: The cases are cut at the SERVED cache's own boundary, not the reference's page. The node reads each case's boundary from the cache itself: the case's prefix is sent and repeated, and the repeat's vllm:prefix_cache_hits are the tokens it read, the deepest block boundary before its end; the prompt is that boundary plus the case's tail, as token ids. A prefix no repeat reads from is doubled into the following cases' prefixes, and the node fails, saying why, if nothing is ever read. At 784 every case's prompt is exactly as before, so T2 and its derivation stand. The server's reported configuration does not carry the page at this base: vllm:cache_config_info reports block_size 8 while the workers align the hybrid page to 784 (800 with MTP) in their own processes (measured). The warm request must itself read that boundary, or the node fails saying so: measured, the earlier procedure (one warm-up, then the warm request) read the cache on only 2 of the reference's 8 cases. Adopted after a registered oracle-first measurement: every rule held on all seven runs, and L1's two passes pass at their own pages on both of their launches.
bars.fidelity_T_superseded: Superseded: kept as the earlier record of one bar on the worst band; test_fidelity_kl reads only fidelity_bands

efficiency.c1_attempts_note: The CANDIDATE's single-request node takes the best of up to this many attempts, with an early exit on the first that meets rho. Throughput and the reference stay one draw. It is upstream's own instrument for this quantity (test_bs_1_speed loops bs_1_speed_attempts = 3 and stops at the first attempt that clears), and it exists because one draw of eight requests failed the HUMAN REFERENCE on another task's speculative recipe (a low-latency S1 ratio of 0.7814). IT IS BIASED UPWARD by construction -- one reference draw against up to three candidate draws -- and the bias scales with the axis's noise, so `first_attempt_ratios` in the record is the unbiased value and is the one to publish. Note also that the promise that any verdict can be recomputed at any rho holds DOWNWARD only: at a higher rho the retries that rho would have triggered were never run, so the best-of-three verdict cannot be recomputed there, while the first-attempt ratio can. On THIS recipe the loop is dead code: the S1 null-ratio sd is 0.0205% over four null samples on two backends, the worst null is 0.9998, and the four candidate S1 ratios measured are 0.9998, 0.9999, 1.0003 and 1.0001 -- nothing comes within 0.19 of rho. The 230 s decode_c1 bound gives the client 200 s, and three 38 s attempts plus overhead is under 130 s, so no deadline moves.

control.what: the reference plus a host-side time.sleep at the top of Model Runner V2's execute_model, inside `if not dummy_run:` after the zero-token early return (gpu/model_runner.py:1517-1539 at the reference).
control.why_that_site: capture, warm-up and profiling reach execute_model only with dummy_run=True, so the sleep is never captured and a graph replay never re-executes it. All four TP workers pay it once per step, in parallel.
control.delay_status: SIZED once, in a dedicated sweep. One launch of the reference from the snapshot with the delay read from a file per step, six values swept, k = 4 timed requests each after two discarded warm-ups, and the sweep returned to 0.0 to show the host had not drifted.
control.expected: separation on S1. At C = 32 async scheduling keeps two batches in flight, so most of the delay may hide behind the longer GPU step; that meets the control's requirement of separation on at least one axis and is recorded as measured.

sizing_measured.instrument: a minimal streaming client using the gate's own definition of S1 -- (n-1)/(t_last - t_first) over the 512 streamed output tokens, counted from return_token_ids, t_first being the first chunk that ADDS A TOKEN. Validated against the engine's own `vllm bench serve` on the same server in the same run: median TPOT 6.768 ms against 6.77 ms, agreement to 0.03%.
sizing_measured.workload: ISL 4,096 token-id prompts, OSL 512, greedy, ignore_eos, a distinct cache_salt per request
sizing_measured.chosen: d = 0.016 s, ratio 0.350 -- about a third -- and below rho/1.5 = 0.533 by a wide margin. Never re-tuned against the gate.
sizing_measured.what_the_sweep_also_measured: EXACTLY 3.4 ms of the delay is hidden at every d: the added TPOT is d - 3.4 ms at 0.004, 0.008, 0.012, 0.016 and 0.024 alike. Under async scheduling a visible step costs about max(GPU step, host work + d), so the baseline's 6.77 ms is the GPU step and the host work is about 3.37 ms, and the delay only starts to show once d exceeds about 3.4 ms. That is the async-overlap model confirmed quantitatively, and it predicts the C = 32 behaviour: the GPU step there is several times longer, so 16 ms of host delay will be largely or wholly hidden and the control is expected to separate on S1 alone, which the control's requirement admits (at least one axis). Measured, not assumed.
sizing_measured.noise_at_bs1: the min-to-max spread within each d is at most 1.5%, and the 0.0 -> 0.0 repeat differs by 0.47%. Well inside the 4% that rho = 0.8 needs for the null invariant rho <= 1 - 5 sigma.
sizing_measured.cross_check: the baseline 147.75 tok/s sits 0.4% from vllm#55890's independently reported B200 TP4 batch-1 figure of 147.2 tok/s (different lengths, later code, torch.compile off, no prefix caching), which is the only other B200 reading that exists for this model.

verifier_version_note: The graded set of this verifier version. The five mixed-turnover records joining-0..3 and replacement are recorded and no longer graded, and the pooled diagnostic S_mt (the mean absolute difference between the served and the teacher-forced log probability over their pooled positions) is recorded beside them: their value is decided by the scheduler's division of the joining request's prefill into mixed iterations, which this task does not fix and a candidate cannot control, so the bars mean_k3 0.1 and max_local_k3 6.0 failed the reference itself in 2 of 20 production runs, 1 of 36 repeats of the node and 4 of 60 in-server repeats under MTP3 (5 of 60 with speculation off), while no registered state-leak control separates on the family. The same workload still runs, the four background records of it and the restored branches keep the same bars, and test_fresh_request_state still grades fresh-request state. Component measurement runs through the engine runner with an independent comparator, three fixed timing matrices, attributable PLE memory and one structural validator for every served observation; the MTP3 component inventory includes mixed speculative/prefill iterations; the two future-alias registry imports are unscored; the deadlines are derived from the public budgets.json; and the candidate's single-request node takes the best of up to c1_attempts draws with an early exit. The paired efficiency gate's two nodes are graded, with the supplied-kernel import among the pass-to-pass set, and the reference is served from a snapshot taken while the verifier image was built.
